As shown in the figure, he wound two coils on the same soft iron ring; coil A is connected to a battery, coil B is connected by a wire, and a small magnetic needle is placed in parallel below the wire. The phenomenon that may be observed in the experiment is
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: At the instant when coil A is connected to the battery, the small magnetic needle will deflect

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Faraday discovered the phenomenon of “magnetism generating electricity” in 1831. As shown in the figure, he wound two coils on the same soft iron ring; coil A is connected to a battery, coil B is connected by a wire, and a small magnetic needle is placed in parallel below the wire. At the instant when coil A and the battery are connected, what phenomenon will appear in the small magnetic needle?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: At the instant when coil A is connected to the battery, the small magnetic needle will deflect
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circular soft iron ring, with coil A wound on the left side, and the two ends of coil A are connected by wires to the battery on the left; coil B is wound on the right side, and coil B is connected into the closed wire circuit on the right side. Below the external wire connected to coil B, a small magnetic needle roughly parallel to the wire is drawn. Reasoning: At the instant when coil A is just connected to the battery, the current in coil A goes from none to existing, and the current changes, so the magnetic flux in the soft iron ring also changes. Coil B is wound on the same soft iron ring, so the magnetic flux passing through coil B changes accordingly, and an induced current will be instantaneously produced in the closed circuit of coil B. When this induced current flows through the wire near the small magnetic needle, it will produce a magnetic field around the wire, causing the small magnetic needle to be acted on by the magnetic field and deflect. Because the induced current appears only when the magnetic flux changes, this kind of deflection is instantaneous.
